title: Nine years with Ella, 1956-65
summary: He was with Ella from 1956 to 1965, with a short spell in Woody Herman's small group in 1959, and she called him in Denver in 1973.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Working with Sinatra: bands, Vegas and the Sands

blocks.x: Yeah. Who was her bass player?
At the time I was telling you about Tommy Flanagan, Benny Moten. He's a bass player.
Is he the son of the other Benny Moten.
No, no, no. No kin whatsoever.
Fancy that.
He was playing bass at the time.
Yeah.
And --
Well, how long did you work on and off with Ella? Did you go out on the road a lot?
Nine years.
I didn't realize that.
Yeah, I was with her clean up to 1965. I joined her in '56.
Well, now, this thing says that you were with Woody Herman in '59.
That was just for a little while, with Woody's small group. And then I went right back with Ella, see.
Well, I never. Fancy that. Well, she must have loved you, Gus.
Well, I stayed with her a long time.
Yeah.
Yeah. I don't know whether she loved me or not, but when I first moved out here in '73, and she played her, well, they sent me a telegram, calling me.
Who, Norman Grant?

Yes, he played with her here in Denver, in '73. And I could have stayed with her, but I was playing with the World's Greatest Jazz Band at the time, which I should have stayed with her, because I went out and made four weeks with it, on the road.
Right then, from --
From here, yeah.
